_doc: The town drunk's notes about town (#1312; DrunkNotes, src/people/drunk_notes.gd; his card: docs/story/people.json town_drunk, 'his pockets hold a stub of chalk and a stub of pencil'). Each: `kind` paper (pencil on a sheet, nailed), bill (a printed-looking bill, tacked), chalk (on the wall itself), scratch (cut into the boards with a knife); `lot`, `a` (m east of its west side), `b` (m off its front: under 0 out on the walk) and `up` (m over the ground there) where a ray goes `into_m` into the lot to find the wall; `size` [w, h] m; `text` what it says (read up close: its words on screen, `read` first), `shows` what's drawn on it if not that; `strokes` a picture's cuts [x0, y0, x1, y1] m from its middle. `appears`: `day` (the nth town day from the badge), `fact` (the story's), `after` a deed of Harlan's (TownDrunk's kinds) `after_h` game hours on. He never names Harlan, Joe is never in it, Rourke and the place in Tennessee not before Payday Night. PROPOSED words, for Sean's script OK (#1150).

notes.read: Chalked on the jail's front wall, in a big careful hand:
notes.text:
The Brevet stands guard at the jail
With a star and a pistol and pail.
When the shooting begins
He'll atone for his sins
In his britches, and never once fail.

notes.read: A sheet nailed by the jail's door, in pencil:
notes.text: NOTICE. The Deputy is IN. If he is OUT he is at the Necessary. If he is at the Necessary DO NOT GO IN. By order, A Veteran.

notes.read: A bill tacked to the store's front, lettered to look printed:
notes.text:
WANTED
for going about dressed as the Law
THE BREVET
answers to Deputy, Farmer and Hey You
walks like he has the Quickstep
REWARD
one clean pair of drawers, little used
apply the door end of the bar

notes.read: Cut into the livery's boards with a knife: a man in a hat with a star as big as his chest, a pistol to his knees, and very little else. Under it:
A sheet pinned by the hotel's door, in pencil:
notes.text: Notice to the Laundress. The Deputy's drawers to be boiled TWICE this week. By request of the Street.

notes.read: Chalked on the saloon's front wall:
notes.text:
THE BREVET'S DRILL
Load. Aim. Fire.
Run.
Change drawers.

notes.read: A sheet nailed up on the saloon's front, in pencil:
notes.text: To the card sharps of Salt Creek. The Deputy is in town. Bring a wheelbarrow for his money. He can't keep his face straight nor his britches clean.

notes.read: Chalked on the saloon's wall, by the door:
notes.text:
THE BREVET'S PROMOTIONS
one glass, corporal
two, sergeant
three, general
four, the floor

notes.read: A sheet tacked up by the store's bench, in pencil:
notes.text: To the Deputy. If you mean to shove a man about, shove ME. I am mostly on the ground already and it saves you the trouble. A Veteran.

notes.read: Chalked on the jail's wall, under the rhyme:
notes.text:
PRISONERS HELD HERE: ONE
LAWMEN HELD HERE: NONE WORTH THE NAME

notes.read: Chalked low on the jail's wall, with an arrow pointing at the walk:
notes.text:
HERE THE LAW FELL DOWN
IT GOT UP AGAIN
MOSTLY

notes._doc: The Clarion's letters column, once the paper exists (Thursday's sheet: not built). No lot: not put up about town; the paper's page will read it.
notes.read: In the Clarion's letters column, under 'From a Correspondent':
notes.text: To the Editor. I call no man sir and I won't start with you. Our Deputy has took to walking the street with his hand on his pistol, which is the only hand on it in town. If a ball is ever fired in his direction I ask the Town to stand well back and upwind. A Veteran of the Union.
